subject: Decision log: which prompt fields are saved (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Erin Martin <erin@healthsynclabs.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:03:00-05:00
Subject: Quick recap + one ask: which prompt fields do you need persisted?

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Per our conversation, HealthSync Labs is evaluating using Redwood for patient-facing triage where prompts will include symptom descriptions and occasional patient identifiers (MRN/email) for lookup flows.

Two quick follow ups so we can get you a concise commitment to share with your security/legal teams:
1) Which prompt elements (if any) does HealthSync need Redwood to persist for your workflows? e.g., full request text, redacted identifiers, or just metadata for billing/observability.
2) Any hard constraints on residency (US-only), retention window (max days), or access controls (e.g., only via delegated service account + egress blocked)?

We attached a proposed data map and a strawman retention clause so you can see typical options. If you can reply with the answers above I'll turn these into a one-page commitment and a line-item for your SOW.

Attachments: redwood-data-map-v2.pdf, proposed-retention-clauses.docx

Thanks — talk soon.

Sergio Alvarez

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 3:03 PM Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Erin —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo time today...

Thanks, Sergio — great demo. A few clarifying items from our side so Legal can evaluate: 
- We cannot accept raw patient identifiers (MRNs, emails) in persistent logs. If anything is stored it must be redacted or tokenized.
- Residency: US-only for any persisted PII or outputs derived from PII.
- Retention: prefer max 30 days for anything that could be reconstructed into patient data; audit logs/metrics for billing are ok longer if irreversibly aggregated.
- Logging controls: we need an option to disable debug/prompt capture for prod, and a clear escalation path (who to contact if an incident is suspected).

Please can you reply with a single-line summary of what Redwood will commit to (e.g., what is stored, where, how long) and any policy exceptions for dedicated/private deployments? Legal would like that before we move to a PO.

— Erin
Erin Martin
Head of Product Security, HealthSync Labs
erin@healthsynclabs.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T19:02:00-05:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + one ask: which prompt fields do you need persisted?

Sergio — looping in Priyom (Product) and Grace (Security) to draft a concise commitment. Our suggested positions below; please confirm before I send to Erin as the formal bullet list.

Proposal (strawman):
- Request payloads (full prompt text) for hosted customers: not persisted by default. We retain an in-flight cache for inference but do not write request text to durable storage unless customer explicitly enables debug capture.
- Optional short-term debug retention (customer opt-in): up to 14 days, US-only storage, encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private.
- Prompt outputs (model responses): ephemeral persistence for 72 hours by default for debugging/replay; can be disabled for Dedicated/Private or turned off via account flag for hosted.
- Billing & telemetry: token counts, route metadata, and aggregate performance metrics retained for 12 months for billing/analytics; these metrics are irreversible aggregates and do not include PII.
- Access & controls: auditor-friendly access logs, RBAC for support engineers, full audit trails; SOC2 Type II in scope; access requires break-glass justification and is recorded.
- Residency: for any persisted debug capture or outputs that could contain PII we will restrict storage to US regions for HealthSync; Dedicated/Private customers can host in their VPC or on-prem.

Attachments: redwood-data-map-v2.pdf (updated to highlight debug capture flow).

If that aligns I'll turn it into the one-line summary Erin requested and add proposed legal text for the SOW.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Decision log: which prompt fields are saved (post-demo follow-up)

Erin — thanks for the quick clarity. Below is the concise commitment from Redwood for HealthSync Labs. This is the summary we can put in an SOW line and Legal can turn into contract language. If that looks right we'll add it to the PO.

Redwood commitment (summary):
- Prompt/request text: not written to durable storage by default for hosted accounts. In-flight caching is used to serve the model but does not persist to long-term storage.
- Optional debug capture: HealthSync may opt in to short-term debug capture. When enabled: stored only in US regions, encrypted at rest, retention max = 14 days, keys customer-managed for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we support KMS-wrapped keys for extra isolation.
- Model outputs (responses): ephemeral persistence for 72 hours by default to support replay/debugging; can be disabled per account (recommended for PHI-sensitive flows).
- Identifiers/PII: Redwood will not persist raw patient identifiers in logs. Any identifier stored for linkage will be hashed with a per-account salt (non-reversible) and stored only if you request it; otherwise we store only metadata.
- Telemetry & billing: token counts, route IDs, and aggregate latency/error metrics retained for 12 months for billing and performance analysis; telemetry is aggregated and does not include raw prompt text or PII.
- Access controls & auditability: all access to persisted debug captures or keys requires RBAC, recorded audit logs, and break-glass justification; SOC2 Type II attestation and routine pen tests apply.
- Residency: any persisted captures for HealthSync will be stored in US-only regions unless you elect Dedicated/Private hosting in your VPC.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the above summary so I can ask Legal to mirror it in the SOW.
2) If you want debug capture enabled for the trial/proof-of-concept, tell us a single point of contact and the desired retention (up to 14 days).
3) If Legal wants tightened language, I can have our contracts team produce a short appendix.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute call to review if helpful.
